explanations.explanation: This feature fires on the boilerplate license/copyright header in source files—i.e. the structured blocks of copyright notices, “Licensed under …” or “GNU GPL/Apache License” lines, version numbers, separators, and related metadata.

This neuron is essentially a “weird‐token” detector: it lights up on subword pieces that are orthographically unusual or outside plain lower-case English—foreign letters (ñ, Cyrillic/Greek/Kanji characters), accented or non-ASCII symbols, uppercase/acronym fragments (& in “S & P”), code-style chunks (“ipl” in “multiplier”), etc. In other words, it signals a switch to a rare/special token or a script/language change.
